short: The world's first operational jet-powered fighter aircraft, offering speed unmatched by conventional Allied fighters.
full:
The Messerschmitt Me 262 "Schwalbe" was a revolutionary German fighter that became the first jet-powered aircraft to see operational service. Powered by two Junkers Jumo 004 turbojets, it was substantially faster than any piston-engined Allied fighter. Development began before the war, but chronic engine unreliability, metallurgical shortages, and Hitler's insistence that it be adapted as a fast bomber severely delayed its combat introduction until April 1944.

When employed as a dedicated interceptor, the Me 262 was devastating against Allied bomber formations, carrying heavy cannons and unguided air-to-air rockets. However, it arrived too late and in too few numbers to alter the course of the war. Suffering from a fragile supply chain, a lack of fuel, and vulnerability during takeoff and landing, most were destroyed on the ground. Its design heavily influenced early post-war jet fighters across the world.
